The Role

As a General Motors Economics Summer Intern, you will support strategic decision-making by analyzing the global macroeconomy, United States and international automotive markets, and key public policy developments.

You will apply your economics training and coding skills to support economic modeling, develop digital tools for internal business partners, and prepare written analysis that translates complex data into clear insights for decision-makers. This is a hands-on, learning-focused opportunity for a graduate student seeking to deepen their understanding of applied macroeconomics and gain experience on an in-house economics team.

The Team

The General Motors Economics team is part of Global Planning and Customer Research. The team supports senior leaders across the company through data-driven analysis of the global economy and automotive industry.The team conducts applied economic research, develops industry forecasts, and analyzes public policy topics to inform General Motors’ business strategy, public policy engagement, and external communications. This internship offers the opportunity to learn applied economics in a real-world setting while working with the Chief Economist and other members of the economics team.

What You’ll Do

During the internship, you will:

- Support analysis of topics such as global and United States economic growth, inflation, labor markets, and household balance sheets.

- Analyze the outlook for the North American and global automotive industries.

- Evaluate the potential effects of public policy changes on General Motors, the automotive industry, and customers.

- Draft concise briefing materials that communicate key economic insights to nontechnical audiences across business units.

- Help build digital tools that automate the distribution of analysis on key economic indicators and automotive industry metrics.

Learning Outcomes

By the end of the internship, you will:

- Gain practical experience applying macroeconomic theory and econometrics to real-world questions facing a global automaker.

- Deepen your understanding of how economic conditions and public policies shape the automotive industry and manufacturing in the United States and abroad.

- Strengthen your coding skills in R, Python, Stata, or similar tools, including documentation and reproducible analysis practices in a business setting.

- Develop experience responsibly applying artificial intelligence tools in a corporate economics environment.

- Learn to translate technical analysis into clear, actionable insights for senior leaders and non-economist audiences.

- Build experience working in a cross-functional corporate environment.

Required Qualifications

- Available to work full-time, 40 hours per week, during the 12 week Summer 2027 internship.

- Currently pursuing a Masters or PhD degree in economics or a closely related field, with rigorous training in macroeconomics and econometrics.

- Master student must be graduating between December 2027 - June 2029.

- PhD student must be graduating between December 2027 -2033.

- Experience using at least one of the following programming languages or tools for data analysis: R, Python, or Stata.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with an ability to communicate clearly and tailor messages to different audiences.

- Interest in the automotive industry, manufacturing, or industrial policy.

- Commitment to learning, openness to feedback, and a collaborative, low-ego approach to teamwork.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience using EViews, MATLAB, or similar economic and statistical tools.

- Familiarity with economic forecasting, applied macroeconomics, econometrics, or automotive industry analysis.

- Experience developing data visualizations, automated reporting, or digital tools for business users.

- Interest in the responsible use of artificial intelligence tools in a corporate economics setting.

- Ability to translate technical analysis into clear, actionable insights for senior leaders and nontechnical audiences.

- Experience collaborating with cross-functional teams, such as finance, vehicle forecasting, public policy, or international markets.

About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Integration, Quality & Manufacturing Engineering Team

Zipline's Integration, Quality & Manufacturing Engineering (IQME) team keeps the factory floor running smoothly. We're responsible for making sure the right parts and materials are always in the right place at the right time, from receiving and warehouse storage, to staging materials right at the production line, to getting finished goods ready to ship.

We work hand-in-hand with Production, Quality, Supply Chain, and Material Planning to build and improve the drones, and we're currently standing up brand-new production lines as we scale fast. We're also focused on using better data from production, inventory, and quality data pulled from systems like our ERP, MES, and traceability tools, to help everyone on the floor make smarter, faster decisions.

About the Data Analytics Intern Role

As a Data Analytics Intern on the IQME team, you'll dive into the data behind how Zipline actually builds and ships its drones, from inventory and materials to production output and quality.

You'll team up with engineers, production leads, quality stakeholders, and leadership to find insights that keep the factory floor running smoothly. Your main focus will be turning data into insights that help people make faster, smarter decisions on the floor.

This role is ideal for someone passionate about data, problem-solving, and seeing their analysis translate directly into real operational impact.
